pr.title: Fix assume and assert in jump threading
pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.summary: JumpThreading had been treating an `Assert` terminator as if it guaranteed `cond == expected`, registering threading opportunities to the matching condition's target. That is unsound because `Assert` can be compiled away at codegen time and therefore is not a semantic assumption. The fix removes the `Assert` special case and ignores `Assert` in the TOFinder, relying instead on real `Assume` facts (a `NonDivergingIntrinsic::Assume` statement); a new custom-MIR test verifies that JumpThreading still threads through an `Assume`.
analysis.originalLogic: In `TOFinder`, the terminator match had a `TerminatorKind::Assert { ref cond, expected, .. }` arm that looked up tracked conditions for `cond.place()`; when a condition matched `expected` (converted to `ScalarInt::TRUE`/`ScalarInt::FALSE`), it called `register_opportunity`, pushing `ThreadingOpportunity { chain: vec![bb], target: c.target }`. The arm was explicitly commented as: `// Treat as an `assume(cond == expected)`.` The `Assume` intrinsic in MIR is instead represented as `StatementKind::Intrinsic(Box::new(NonDivergingIntrinsic::Assume(op)))`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect rewrite was to thread control flow through an `Assert` terminator by redirecting its successor to the branch target corresponding to the asserted condition (`c.target` for a condition matching `expected`). This treats the assert as a guaranteed semantic fact and skips the path that would be taken if the condition were false. Because an `Assert` can be a no-op at codegen time, the condition is not actually guaranteed, so the redirected edge can reach a block/value that is wrong for the real runtime condition. The corrected code instead does `TerminatorKind::Assert { .. } => None` with the comment `// Ignore, as this can be a no-op at codegen time.` and keeps threading only through genuine `Assume` facts.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR function bodies processed by JumpThreading that contain an `Assert` terminator whose condition place has tracked equality/range conditions, where the assert's `expected` value matches one of those conditions and the same place is later branched on (or a target associated with the condition is otherwise reachable). Also relevant: bodies containing an `Assume` intrinsic statement followed by a `switchInt` on the assumed boolean. The test body uses `match a { 7 => bb1, _ => bb2 }`, `Assume(b); Goto(bb3)`, and `match b { false => bb4, _ => bb5 }`.
analysis.trigger: While flooding/visiting a block reached as a target, the terminator is `TerminatorKind::Assert`; `cond` is a place with tracked conditions; one tracked scalar condition equals the assert's `expected` boolean. In the old code this registers a threading opportunity to `c.target`. For the retained positive behavior, the block instead contains an `Assume` statement on a boolean that is subsequently used in a `switchInt`.
preconditions: JumpThreading's TOFinder is traversing a MIR body and reaches a block whose terminator is an `Assert` (old code registered an opportunity) or an `Assume` statement (new/tested behavior).
For the Assert bug: the assert condition is a place tracked in the condition state, and its expected value matches a tracked condition, so the old `register_opportunity` path fires.
The assert may be compiled away at codegen time, so `cond == expected` is not a semantic invariant.
For the Assume test: an `Assume(b)` is followed by a `switchInt(b)`, so JumpThreading can retarget the edge after the assume to the branch matching `b == true`.
The regression test is built with `#[custom_mir(dialect = "runtime", phase = "post-cleanup")]` and run under both panic-abort and panic-unwind variants.
pitfalls: Do not treat an `Assert` terminator as equivalent to `assume(cond == expected)`; the assert may be a codegen no-op.
Do not confuse the `Assume` intrinsic statement (`NonDivergingIntrinsic::Assume`) with an `Assert` terminator; only the former is a semantic assumption.
Do not infer that the old behavior was correct merely because a test file named `jump_threading.assume...` exists; the new test covers `Assume`, not `Assert`.
Do not claim the test demonstrates reproduction of the Assert bug; the supplied patch adds a positive `Assume` threading test but no explicit `Assert` regression case.
Borrowing restrictions and post-copy overwrites are separate conditions; do not conflate them with the Assert-versus-Assume soundness issue.
analysis.testStrategy: Use custom MIR to isolate the transformation. For the intended positive case, build a body where one predecessor executes `Assume(b)` and then `Goto(bb3)`, while `bb3` does `switchInt(b) -> [0: bb4, otherwise: bb5]`; assert via CHECK lines that JumpThreading keeps `assume(_2); goto -> bb6;` and appends `bb6: goto -> bb5;`, showing the assume-derived edge goes to the true branch while the original `bb3` switch remains. Run under both panic-abort and panic-unwind because the pass emits separate diffs. For the fixed Assert bug, construct a variant containing an `Assert` terminator whose condition/expected match a tracked condition and verify the pass does not register a threading opportunity to that condition's target; compare actual value assignments/edges before and after, not just test names or comments. Use `// EMIT_MIR jump_threading.assume.JumpThreading.diff` style MIR dumps and CHECK-LABEL/CHECK-NEXT to pin block edges.
evidence: Fix assume and assert in jump threading
Do not thread through Assert terminator.
